page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized instance built on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs allocated across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). Compute resources are dedicated, featuring a cache hierarchy that includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache per core. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates advanced instruction set extensions including Intel AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution units, AES cryptography, and SHA-NI acceleration. The instance does not bundle local NVMe SSD storage or attached GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core CPU efficiency alongside lower multi-core scaling and memory throughput profiles. The single-core stress-ng rating of 1620.59 and Geekbench single-core score of 1635.0 place the instance in middle performance tiers. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression at 25.97 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 6.78 GB/sec perform consistently. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks show reduced relative output, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 3703.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6115.19, reflecting the physical 2-core boundary. Memory subsystem performance remains constrained, recorded at 27.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 21.03 GB/sec for writes.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-4 is tailored for workloads that require dedicated CPU compute and modern vector extensions without requiring high memory capacity or attached disk arrays. It delivers effective prompt processing and text generation speeds for small language models and performs reliably for basic web traffic serving. However, memory-bound database operations and highly parallel multi-threaded build jobs may experience performance bottlenecks due to the lower memory bandwidth and 8 GB RAM limitation. Recommended deployments include lightweight web applications, single-threaded microservices, and entry-level algorithmic processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor. Built on a 2 physical core topology with 2 threads per core, it offers 105 MB of L3 cache and support for advanced instruction sets including Intel AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no attached local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average single-threaded CPU capability, static web serving throughput of 6.78 GB/sec, and steady small-model LLM text generation. However, multi-core scaling, memory bandwidth, and database operations score lower due to the limited physical core count and 2.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation. The c3-highcpu-4 offers a balanced profile for lightweight single-threaded microservices, basic web hosting, and entry-level vector-accelerated tasks where large memory capacity and high multi-core parallelism are not required.
